descriptionChirho: The core Qal active sense of deliberately choosing or selecting a person, place, or thing, covering all finite verb forms, imperatives, infinitives, cohortatives, and active participles across all persons and numbers.

The Qal passive participle used substantively or attributively to designate persons or groups as chosen or elect, rendered in Arabic as مُخْتَار, in Korean as 선택된/뽑힌, and in Swahili as wateule/waliochaguliwa.

The Qal passive participle used as a quality adjective meaning choice, prime, or excellent, distinguished by Arabic بَحُور, Korean 뛰어나네 (outstanding), and Swahili bora (best), describing inherent superior quality rather than the act or result of election.
The Nifal stem expressing the passive or reflexive sense of being chosen or being preferred, with Arabic مُخْتارٌ and Korean 택함을 받다 (to receive choosing) and Swahili huchaguliwa (is chosen).
The Pual intensive passive form attested only as a ketiv reading, representing a scribal or dialectal variant of the passive sense of being chosen.
